Hi John,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — appreciate you and the team taking the time. Per our conversation I pulled together a concise mutual action plan (MAP) to line up legal/procurement milestones and an aggressive close window. The goal is to have a signed order form in place so you can start trialing Dedicated capacity by mid-March.

High-level sequence I propose:
- Week 1 (Feb 15–21): Redwood sends updated MSA + DPA redlines; Acme reviews and returns cohort-level comments.
- Week 2 (Feb 22–28): Parallel negotiation — Legal (MSA) + Privacy (DPA); Procurement to review order form terms.
- Week 3 (Mar 1–7): Finalize MSA and DPA; sign via DocuSign.
- Week 4 (Mar 8–14): Execute order form / PO, provisioning and onboarding.

Can you confirm whether this sequencing works for Procurement and Legal at your side? If Acme needs different ordering — e.g., DPA first, MSA after — we can adapt but would like to understand any gating items (SOC2, IP addenda, data residency clauses, specific insurer wording).

Attachments: initial MAP (inline below), checklist of docs we typically provide, and our SOC2 report (link/attachment).

Proposed next step: 30-minute alignment call Friday Feb 13 to lock milestones — are you available 10am PT?

Thanks,

Folks — quick note from legal/ops on sequencing and risks:

1) Recommended sequencing to preserve momentum:
   - Step 1: Exchange and agree DPA redlines (privacy items that are often quick: subprocessor list, SCCs or EU transfer mechanism).
   - Step 2: Agree MSA commercial terms (liability caps, indemnities, SLO language).
   - Step 3: Execute both MSA + DPA via DocuSign.
   - Step 4: Issue order form / PO referencing executed MSA.

2) If Acme needs an order form ASAP to reserve capacity, we can accept a signed PO referencing the current MSA draft and include an explicit contingency clause that final payment/activation is subject to executed MSA/DPA within 30 days. That’s a standard approach we’ve used with other enterprise customers.

3) Turnaround expectations: Redwood legal can do an initial pass on Acme redlines within 3 business days for DPA and 5 business days for MSA, provided we have the redlines in a single review package. Please send tracked changes to dev.patel@redwood.com.

4) Required evidence for Procurement: SOC2 report (attached) and a list of subprocessor endpoints. I’ve attached our SOC2-report-2024.pdf and an internal redlines checklist.

If Acme Legal is available, propose a joint legal sync Tuesday Feb 23 at 10am PT to go through DPA redlines.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
